blocks.text: This letter sets out the terms on which the firm will review the patent portfolio of {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}. It follows our conversations this spring and the schedule of matters your office sent afterward, and it records what we will review, who will carry the work, what we will need from you, and the commercial terms that govern the engagement. When you have signed and returned the enclosed copy, this letter becomes the agreement between us and replaces anything discussed before it.

The engagement is a structured review of the patents and pending applications in the portfolio, taken one family at a time. For each family we will reconcile the docketed dates against the office record, review the prosecution history and the claims as they now stand, and identify any filing, response, or decision that is coming due. You will receive a written review organized the same way, family by family, setting out what we found and the questions we believe you should decide.

Some work sits outside this review and is available under a separate engagement if you ask for it. Under this letter we are not prosecuting new applications, responding to office actions, filing continuations, or preparing a freedom-to-operate opinion; where the review reaches a matter that calls for one of those, we will tell you and stop rather than begin work you have not authorized. The review is not an opinion that any patent is valid, infringed, or clear to practice, and it should not be read or relied upon as one.

We work from the office record and your own files rather than from a summary prepared by someone else. Heather Munoz will take the families in an order we set against the docket, so that the matters closest to a deadline are reviewed first and nothing urgent waits behind something that can wait. We keep the docket at the center of the work, and the review is built to surface any date at risk early enough that you can act on it deliberately rather than under pressure. You will hear from us on a regular schedule, and every update will be tied to the matter it concerns.

Heather Munoz, a partner in the prosecution group, leads the review and is responsible for what we conclude and for what we send you. Kelly Snyder, a patent agent, keeps the portfolio docket current and reconciles the dates the review relies on. Amanda Schwartz, an associate, prepares the family-by-family write-ups under Heather Munoz's review. I read the completed review before it reaches you, as I do with everything that leaves this office, and I am the person to call if at any point you are not satisfied with the work or with the people doing it.

We have run our conflicts check for this matter and are clear to act for you. Should a conflict arise later, whether from a new client or a change in an existing one, we will bring it to you promptly and address it as our professional obligations require, which may include declining part of the work. We will not take on a matter adverse to your interests in this portfolio while this engagement is open.

Work commences on {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}, subject to your signature on this letter and to our receiving the portfolio schedule, access to the prosecution files, and confirmation of who at {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} we should coordinate with on individual matters. We will not begin billing before that date. If you need us to hold a specific date in the meantime, tell us and we will docket it so that it is not lost while the letter is in transit.

Our fee for the review, and the basis on which it is fixed, are stated on the signature page, which counsel for each side has executed separately, and they are not repeated here. We invoice monthly for the work of the preceding month, and each invoice is payable within thirty days of its date. Work that falls outside the review is not undertaken on assumption: if you ask for something this letter does not cover, we will quote it and wait for your written authorization before we begin. If an invoice remains unpaid beyond its terms, we may suspend work on the matter after written notice to you; because the review runs against live dockets, we will identify any date then at risk before we stop, so that a billing dispute never becomes a lost deadline.

This agreement takes effect on the date you sign below and continues until the review is delivered and our final invoice paid. Either of us may end it earlier on written notice to the other. If the engagement ends before the review is complete, you will owe us for the work performed and the expenses incurred to that point, and we will deliver our work in the state it then stands together with a written note of what remains open and any date we know to be approaching. An unfinished review is not a conclusion and should not be relied on as one.

We will hold what you give us in confidence and use it only for this engagement, and access within the firm is limited to the people named above and to those whose work on the matter requires it. We will not disclose your information outside the firm without your consent, except where a court or another authority with jurisdiction compels it, and in that event we will tell you first if we are free to do so. Our written analysis is prepared as privileged attorney work product for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}; to keep that protection intact, please limit its circulation on your side and do not forward it outside the company without speaking to us first. These obligations continue after the engagement ends.

Our liability to you arising out of this engagement, whether framed in contract or in negligence, will not exceed the total fees you pay us under it, except in the case of our fraud or willful misconduct. Neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss, including lost profits or lost opportunity, whether or not the possibility was known in advance. Our review rests on the accuracy and completeness of the records you and the patent offices provide; where those records are wrong or incomplete, the consequences of the error are not ours to carry, though we will tell you as soon as we have reason to doubt what we have been given.

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our office sits, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Before either of us begins a proceeding, we will try to resolve the dispute through discussion between people with authority to settle it. This letter and its signature page are the whole of the agreement on their subject, and either may be changed only in a writing signed by both of us.

If these terms match your understanding, please sign both copies where indicated, keep one for your file, and return the other to my office. If any term does not, telephone me and we will settle it before you sign. The one thing I need from you to start the review is the signed letter; send it back and we will docket the portfolio and begin the first family.

To: Heather Munoz, Amanda Schwartz
From: Kelly Snyder
Re: {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} patent portfolio review, kickoff and docket

This opens the {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} portfolio review and sets the work for the first weeks. The engagement is a family-by-family review of the portfolio: reconcile the docketed dates against the office record, check the prosecution history and the current claim scope, and flag anything coming due. We are engaged as of {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}, and the docket is the first priority.

Before any substantive review, two constraints hold. No date can slip while we get organized, and every conclusion has to trace to the office record rather than to a prior summary. Keep both in mind as you work.

The scope is the existing portfolio only. We are not prosecuting new filings or responding to office actions under this engagement; if the review turns up something that needs either, it goes to Heather Munoz and then to {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} as a separate question, not into this work. The output is a single written review, organized family by family, that the client can act on. Keep your notes in that structure from the start, so assembling the review at the end is collation and not reconstruction.

One master date list governs the work. I keep it, it lives on the matter docket, and every date any of us relies on has to be on it and reconciled against the office record. If a date is not on the list, treat it as unconfirmed and check it before you act.

items: 1. Docket audit. Kelly Snyder pulls every family in the portfolio and reconciles each docketed date against the office record. Any discrepancy is logged the day it is found, with the source noted so a second reader can confirm it. The audit closes only when every family reconciles.

2. File-history reconciliation. Amanda Schwartz works through the prosecution histories family by family, confirms the current claim set, and flags gaps or missing documents for retrieval. She starts with the larger families, where the histories are longest. Missing documents are logged and requested the same week.

3. Substantive review. Heather Munoz reviews each family for claim scope and prosecution posture, in the order the docket sets, and owns what we conclude. Nothing about scope is treated as settled until she has read the file. A family is not marked done until her notes are in.

4. Client updates. Status goes to Gary Smith against the matter on a regular cadence, and every note is tied to the family it concerns. Any date at risk is reported the day we see it, not at the next scheduled update. We keep the client current even in the weeks the news is thin.
1. Kelly Snyder completes the docket audit for the full portfolio and circulates the reconciled list of dates, marking any that are close. Discrepancies go on the list with the office record cited.
2. Amanda Schwartz begins the file histories with the largest family and reports gaps as she finds them, so retrieval starts before the review reaches that family.
3. Heather Munoz sets the review order against the docket once the audit is in, urgent families first, and circulates the sequence to the team.
4. We confirm the standing update slot and the format with Gary Smith, so the client cadence is set from the start and the first status goes out on time.

If a date looks wrong or tight, raise it the same day rather than holding it for the next scheduled check. I will reconcile the master date list against the office record each week until the audit is closed, and I will flag anything that has moved.

I am opening this thread so our updates on the {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} portfolio review stay in one place and the record runs in order against the matter. For the file, the working contacts are set: Gary Smith, General Manager, on your side, and on ours Heather Munoz, who leads the review, and Amanda Schwartz, who is reconciling the prosecution files with me.

We have made a start. The patent families are pulled and on the docket, and Amanda Schwartz is reconciling each file history against the office record before Heather Munoz begins her first review pass. Nothing in the portfolio is date-critical in this window, and I will flag any deadline the moment one comes into view. You will hear from us on a set cadence, and each note will be tied to the family it concerns.

One request before the work goes further. Please confirm who at {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} we should coordinate with on individual matters, and who holds authority to sign a filing if a response falls due mid-review, so we route it correctly the first time. A name and title for each is enough for now.

Noted, and thank you. For the file, I have recorded your confirmation that Gary Smith signs any filing that falls due for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} during the review, so a response can go out on time if one comes up before we finish.

Kelly Snyder is out on the docket calendar this week, so I am carrying the thread. Amanda Schwartz has finished reconciling the file histories, and I have started the substantive review, taking the families one at a time. Nothing is date-critical yet.
I will send the first family summary once I have been through the largest one. If a deadline surfaces before then, you will hear from me the same day.

blocks.text: The review is on schedule and no docket date is at risk. Kelly Snyder has closed the docket audit for the full portfolio, and the dates now reconcile against the office record, with two corrections found during the audit entered and cross-checked by a second reader. Amanda Schwartz has completed the file histories for the larger families, and the remaining families are in progress. Roughly half the portfolio has had a first substantive read; the rest is sequenced and waiting.

Heather Munoz walked the group through the families reviewed so far. Two families carry claims broader than the prosecution history comfortably supports, and both are marked for a closer read before any conclusion is offered; nothing about claim scope was represented as settled at this session. A third family turned up a term amended during prosecution that narrows the claim more than the file summary suggested, and that one is flagged for the same closer read.

Gary Smith asked that the families most important to the company's current work be moved up in the review order, and the team agreed to resequence accordingly. He also asked when he could expect the first written summaries. Heather Munoz committed to sending the summary for the largest family once its closer read is complete, and to holding any scope conclusion until then.

The docket carried the meeting. Heather Munoz confirmed that every family now sits on the matter docket with its dates reconciled, and that the two corrections have been entered and confirmed against the office record. Gary Smith asked how the firm guards against a missed date. Heather Munoz described the weekly reconciliation and the rule that any date in question is raised the day it is found, not at the next scheduled review.

Two items are open. Kelly Snyder is confirming the chain of one continuation whose recorded priority date does not match the file, and Amanda Schwartz is retrieving two documents missing from the histories on the smaller families. Neither affects a live deadline, and both are due before the next session. Until the continuation chain is confirmed, its recorded priority date stays marked unconfirmed on the master list, and no conclusion for that family rests on it.
